# Requirements Document: The boarding pass credential

## Introduction

The guide models a bar-coded boarding pass as an mdoc with one namespace and
one data element, a text string that follows IATA Resolution 792 (§4.1.2).
The resolution is not available to this project, so the rules take what it
decides as a parameter.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneId/BoardingPass.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/BoardingPass.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet. *Sources* lists the sections of the guide each rule was written from, *External specifications* lists the specifications it relies on and whether this project has read each, and *Confirmation* says whether anyone outside the model has confirmed the rule as written.

## Requirements

### Requirement OID-103

**User Story:** As an airport touchpoint, I want every boarding pass credential I accept to carry one boarding pass string in the standard format, so that I can process it as I process a printed or mobile bar code.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL accept a credential as a boarding pass only when it meets every requirement the guide places on one. (Lean: `BoardingPass.violations`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.2 Boarding pass](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard)

**External specifications:** IATA Resolution 792 (BCBP), the resolution as a whole (not read); IETF RFC 8949 (CBOR), text string (tstr) (read); ISO/IEC 18013-5:2021, §6.3.1, §8.3.1, §8.3.2 (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF the document type of a credential is not the boarding pass document type THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as a boarding pass.
   - OID-103.1, proven: proven theorem `boardingPass_docType`; proven theorem `not_photoid_and_boardingPass`; example `documentTypes`
2. IF a boarding pass lacks the boarding pass namespace THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-103.2, proven: proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; example `boardingPassStrings`
3. IF a boarding pass lacks the boarding pass string THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-103.3, proven: proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; example `boardingPassStrings`
4. IF the boarding pass string is not a text string THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the boarding pass.
   - OID-103.4, proven: proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; proven theorem `boardingPass_strings_follow`; example `boardingPassStrings`
5. IF the boarding pass string does not follow IATA Resolution 792 THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the boarding pass.
   - OID-103.5, proven: proven theorem `boardingPass_has_string`; proven theorem `boardingPass_strings_follow`; example `boardingPassStrings`
6. IF a boarding pass carries a namespace or a data element the guide does not list THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it.
   - OID-103.6, open: open theorem `boardingPass_only_listed`; example `boardingPassWithExtraNameSpace`

#### Open question on OID-103.6

> An accepted boarding pass carries one namespace with one data element, the
> boarding pass string.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide lists one namespace with one data
> element and says a later version may add a namespace for separate data
> elements.  It does not say whether a boarding pass may carry one today.
> Under the reading that it may, a boarding pass with a second namespace is
> accepted, and a relying party cannot tell what a boarding pass credential
> contains from the guide alone.  The example
> `boardingPassWithExtraNameSpace` shows it.  May a boarding pass
> credential carry a namespace or a data element the guide does not list?
